claims.text: The high-entropy alloy and duplex stainless steel initially have no pre-existing oxide enrichment.
Rapid heating–quenching cycling triggers formation of a passivating oxide film on the high-entropy alloy.
The passivating oxide film is stabilized by high entropy.
The passivating oxide film self-regenerates during wear events.
The oxide film remains chemically inert under simultaneous corrosive and mechanical stress.
The oxide film remains mechanically adherent under simultaneous corrosive and mechanical stress.
Rapid thermal cycling promotes nucleation of metastable oxide phases.
High configurational entropy of the alloying elements stabilizes the metastable oxide phases.
Rapid regeneration of the passivating film reduces abrasive damage.
Rapid regeneration of the passivating film reduces corrosive attack.
After matched thermal cycling and tribocorrosion testing, the high-entropy alloy will have lower wear volume than duplex stainless steel.
After matched thermal cycling and tribocorrosion testing, the high-entropy alloy will have lower corrosion current density than duplex stainless steel.
The regenerated passivating film provides simultaneous protection against mechanical and chemical degradation.
The prediction should hold when rapid thermal cycling promotes oxide-film formation in the corrosive environment.
The protective mechanism may fail when the medium or thermal-cycling parameters do not favor film formation.
The protective mechanism may fail when the alloy composition does not support oxide-film adherence.
The magnitude and reproducibility of protection may vary with alloy composition and testing conditions.
